reference_items.stem:
Get to 20 Number Game

Two children, Joan and Herbert, are learning to play a game “Get to 20.” Here are the rules for the game.

GET TO 20
RULES

Pick Tiles: Each player draws three number tiles.

Add Tiles: Each player places the three tiles to make an addition problem with the sum total closest to 20.

For example, here are four ways a player who draws [1] , [4] , and [5] could place the tiles:

  [5] [1]          [4] [5]          [1] [5]             [1]
+     [4]    or  +     [1]    or  +     [4]    or     + [5]
---------        ---------        ---------         + [4]
       55               46               19         -----
                                                       10

This player should choose to show the addition problem
  15
+  4
----
  19
because 19 is the total closest to 20.

Joan and Herbert played the game “Get to 20.”

Joan picked [2] , [7] , and [9] . Herbert picked [1] , [3] , and [6] .

B. What is the addition problem that Herbert could make with his number tiles that gives a total closest to 20? Be sure to include the total.

descriptors: 19 without addition statement shown
13 + 6 OR 16 + 3 but 19 not shown
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

The figure shows how Mary spent her time one day.

[Image: Pie chart showing how Mary spent her time]

What percent of time altogether did she spend playing and doing homework?
reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart showing how Mary spent her time one day, divided into five labeled sectors:
- "Homework 10%": from the 12 o'clock vertical radius clockwise to roughly 1 o'clock.
- "Sleeping & Resting 40%": from roughly 1 o'clock clockwise to the 6 o'clock vertical radius.
- "Going to School 25%": from the 6 o'clock vertical radius clockwise to the 9 o'clock horizontal radius.
- "Eating 10%": from the 9 o'clock horizontal radius clockwise to roughly 10 o'clock.
- "Playing 15%": from roughly 10 o'clock clockwise to the 12 o'clock vertical radius.

What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
